title: Deponia: The Complete Journey
text: "Hilarious." It's a very original Point and Click adventure game. It's full of that kind of charm that you'd only find in Pn'Cs. My biggest issue with the game so far is that it heavily drags on in some areas due to the nonsensical nature of the puzzle solving. If you're as bad at point and clicks as I am, then prepare to use an online walkthrough to get through most of the game, and turn off the music at some points (it get's unbearable, sometimes). These problems are somewhat subjective, though, as other people may actually find these puzzles to be a breeze. Thankfully, these issues are worth soldering on for. The characters have this very hilarious banter that keeps me playing. There's just something to their wit that I just find really charming. They're all likeable butt heads. I had this one issue with the graphics, they'd be glitchy and moving around awkwardly, but I fixed it by turning off texture compression in the settings menu. Once that was fixed, I was suprised and relieved to see that the aesthetic of the game is vibrant and well designed. I've never played The Monkey Island games but from what I've seen; this game looks a lot like it. If you're looking for a nice, relaxing, funny game that tells a great story (and actually has a suprisingly unpreachy earth message), then I don't see why you shouldn't pick this game up. Especially on sale. 8/10 (on sale, due to myself needing a guide to advance) :]

title: Deponia: The Complete Journey
text: A throwback to adventure gaming, highlighting both the high and low points of the genre, but saves face with the charm of its utterly charmless hero. Pros: Well voice acted and witty writing throughout. Surprisingly engaging story and characters. Most of the logic puzzles are intuitive and fairly challenging. Art style of the game is unique and whimsicle, squeezing a substancial amount of creative juice from the trash planet motif. Cons: Most of the designated puzzles (switch puzzles, slider puzzles and whatnot) distract from the flow of the game rather than enhance it and the game would be stronger without them. Some technical issues (Once I was forced to download and install a save game file in order to progress due to a crash glitch). Characters will break character at times to keep the narrative going or in an attempt to shock the player with a plot twist (Goal in particular tends to suffer from this trend a lot). Game's treatment of women in general might cause consternation and seems less ironic and more unintended (Your first clue being that the female costar is named Goal). Would recommend to: Monkey Island fans specifically or fans of LucasArts or Sierra adventure games in general, who don't mind having to google up a working save file. Anyone looking for a genuinely charming tale of a misanthropic dreamer and his unfortunate coterie (who, again, can find that save file).

title: Deponia: The Complete Journey
text: Deponia: The Complete Journey is a really good game and is highly recommended to anyone who enjoys adventure games. I'd give it a 7/10. Pros: + Very lengthy and worth the price - ~30 hours + Hilarious most of the time + Excellent voice acting + Some very nice puzzles + Well thought out world Cons - Puzzles can be obtuse - Mini-game puzzles are mainly terrible - Main character can be too much of a jerk to be likable - Unsatisfying ending to series This is the closest to a Monkey Island game we have had in quite some time(well, other than Tales of Monkey Island). It's nice to see a company that continues to make adventure games, a genre that is still active, but less so than in the past. Other than some incredibly obtuse and unsatisfying puzzles, the majority of the game is  a lot of fun. I laughed, thought hard, solved puzzles, and had a smile on my face most of the 30 hour playtime. I paid $6 for this game it was worth every penny. It has its drawbacks, but its positives far outweigh the negatives.

title: Deponia: The Complete Journey
text: 9/10 The Deponia trilogy is like the point and click games we grew up on as children injected with a triple shot of espresso, irreverent adult humor, and a couple doses of steroids just for fun. The environment and artwork is quirky and the puzzles take a lot of thought but are well planned out and definitely aren't traditional. Deponia and Chaos on Deponia were my favorite to play, as they also seemed to follow a better train of thought as far as puzzles went. Goodbye Deponia, while it had its good moments, had a couple, shall I say, "awkward" puzzles, which seemed to actually take away from the game for me. It was also the hardest to follow, as some of the puzzles were a tad buggy or didn't make sense. If you need help at all in any of the games, Gameboomers has great walkthroughs for all of them. The walkthrough was especially helpful at times in Goodbye Deponia. I would definitely recommend purchasing all three of these games, because not knowing what happens to Rufus, Goal, and Deponia is like watching Firefly and then never watching Serenity. Because these games have no ESRB ratings, I (as always) rate it myself, and do my best to remain true to the ESRB guidelines. title: Deus Ex: Revision
text: People seem to hate this mod for whatever reason....its a MOD for crying out loud, if you don't like it, play the original you idiots! Nothing's changed there, its just that the Mod is SELECTABLE!...Ahem getting off track here. This review is going to be long so if you are not interested in the 'wall of text' then look at the bottom of this for the TL;DR summary...Now with that said and done, from my mountain stronghold I write this with no fear of retaliation! Deus Ex: Revision is as the title suggests, a revision of Deus Ex's graphics, the game is the same but it looks much more polished, the gameplay is as solid as ever and while the remade music CAN put some people off, I don't have issue with it as it manages to maintain, if not at times, IMPROVE that feeling that you want in a Cyberpunk Game. It has flaws, the aforementioned soundtrack being offputting to others, the fact that there is added bits in levels CAN lead to some serious confusion, I almost never found the crowbar you could find early until I saw the hut they placed. And that's about it with flaws for me...I may not be all that qualified to say flaws given my time with it but just letting that out for ya. Anyone who seems to complain that it does things too new, hey I know purists when I see them, JUST PLAY THE ORIGINAL GAME! You had to have it in the first place in order to get the mod so just play that, and even then you can lower the textures and change things back to normal in the options menu. The new bits in levels actually adds character to them, the aforementioned hut being one along with how you find Smuggler...it was almost impossible for me to find him in the original game but I took WAY LONGER finding him this time round because I didn't know that there is a building that is surrounded by cops, near a chopshop! Thankfully not only did this allow me to see in detail the fact that there were MORE buildings to enter, but I think I can find that more competently now :D The Graphics actually look nice and give an actual feel for the characters, the actors have not changed which is fine, and overall, for a remake? This is solid....Props to the fans who made it, give them some respect as I, nor alot of you, know how much time it takes to write code and edit bits IN said code! Again getting off track here.... Overall I say this with as much confidence as possible: Go play this game, you will not regret it as even if you don't like it? Your wallet will remain untouched as Revision is FREE and you can just play the vanilla version VERY easily because you can select which version you want to play! TL;DR: I recommend this game, it has only 2 nagging flaws that I saw, 1 if you like the redone music, and its DEUS EX at it's core, just with more stuff to see.

title: Deus Ex: Revision
text: It doesn't take long to see where changes have been made to the venerable Deus Ex. The music is going to be your first cue. Familiar themes remixed in ways that rip you right out of that immersion when they flow straight into unfamiliar. But you can revert to the original soundtrack. Then you have the character models. Smoother, rounder, making everyone look like they have helium filled balloons for heads. But you can revert those. Modded gameplay. Skill points for being brutal, superfluous weapons, new combat options. But you can revert that. Modded levels. Know a stealthy path through Liberty Island? Nope, there are more guards watching the stealthy path than patrolling in the open. Oh, and about half the ammo has been removed. The thing that really killed it for me was "Corporal Maxwell" on Liberty Island, a duplicate of Corporal Collins. Suddenly it wasn't about enjoying a classic game with new surprises, it was about judging wether the facelift was worth cloning one of the few unique characters in UNATCO HQ. If you  can immerse yourself in Deus Ex, give Revision a pass. It looks pretty, certainly, but every few steps you'll be hit by something that reminds you that you're playing something different, and suddenly that precious immersion is gone.

title: Devil Daggers
text: One of the best shooters I've played. Devil Daggers is the perfect example of minimalism in game design. Limited graphics. Empty arena. Enemies move in predictable manners. Only one weapon. No health, no ammo, and only one power-up. No music! It's a niche, I admit. If you're expecting anything more than an arcade-style score attack, you'll be rather miffed. For those after a real, intense, incredibly immersive challenge, this is it. + Incredibly smooth controls, all rebindable. + Reviewer has experienced no technical issues on a mid-range NVIDIA (920M). Smooth framerate. + Amazing sound. (Headphones are a MUST, or a surround-sound speaker system.) + Intuitive movement. Straferunning and rocket-jumping has been simulated in engine. + Replays and leaderboard built into engine. All scores on leaderboard have a replay attached! - Only one level and one mode. Flat arena, timed survival. - Graphically busy in late-game or when many enemies spawn. - No character progression, story, upgrades, cosmetics. Only one Steam achievement. I'd love to see an update (or hell, a DLC) that adds an alternative arena. Maybe another dozen enemies in a secondary game mode? What's here is great, but if setting high scores has never been your thing then you're going to get tired fast.
